note: Bahrain: a work permit is the Labour Market Regulatory Authority's consent to an employer to employ a given foreign worker (Order No. 76 of 2008, art. 1). Foreigners who come for occasional, temporary work for an employer, such as markets, exhibitions, celebrations, festivals or ceremonies, for no more than fifteen days from the start of the work, aren't subject to the LMRA law, provided the employer has the permits the activity needs (Order No. 2 of 2013, art. 1): so 15 days without the permit. Both read on the LMRA's legislation pages through archive.org (snapshots of 22 May 2024 and 12 January 2026; the second still lists Order No. 2 of 2013 among its resolutions), since lmra.gov.bh refuses this client. GCC citizens' position isn't modelled apart, and the entry visa isn't modelled.

sources.title: Labour Market Regulatory Authority, Order No. (2) of 2013 on temporary works of foreigners (archive.org snapshot of 12 January 2026)
sources.said: Foreigners who come to the Kingdom for the purpose of accomplishing temporary works shall not be subject to the provisions of the Labor Market Regulatory Authority Law, when the following controls and conditions exist: The works performed by the foreign workers for an employer are occasional and temporary such as establishment of markets, exhibitions, celebrations, festivals, ceremonies or other activities. The execution of works performed by the foreign workers for an employer shall not be for a period exceeding fifteen days from the date of commencement of the work.

sources.title: Labour Market Regulatory Authority, Decision No. (76) of 2008 on work visas of foreign employees (archive.org snapshot of 22 May 2024)
sources.said: Work Permit or Permit: A permission issued by the Authority granting a consent to an employer to employ a certain foreign or expatriate worker subject to the provisions of the Law of Labour Market Regulatory and the provisions stated in this Order.
